UNDER THE HOOD

A smarter way there.

See exactly how A* finds the fastest route through the road graph.

A* SEARCH ALGORITHM

Good directions begin
with a good estimate.

f(n) = g(n) + h(n)

g(n) is the travel time from the starting point to the current node.

h(n) estimates the time remaining using straight-line distance and the maximum demo speed of 50 km/h.

The algorithm explores the node with the lowest f(n), updates its neighbours, and repeats until the destination is reached.

Traffic increases road costs. Closed roads are excluded. The heuristic stays a lower bound, so A* returns the minimum travel-time path on this graph.

THE PROJECT

Meet AmbuTrack.

An understandable, hands-on ambulance dispatch project.

Built to learn. Designed to demonstrate.

AmbuTrack combines ambulance assignment, hospital selection, route planning and animated tracking in one student project. Its A* implementation runs directly in JavaScript, with no paid APIs or external dependencies.

What works

A* search on a weighted road graph, traffic and road-closure scenarios, automatic unit assignment, two-stage trip simulation, availability controls, search traces and CSV export.

What is simulated

The map, hospitals, crews, traffic and vehicle positions are illustrative. There is no real GPS tracking, emergency dispatch, hospital integration, account system or shared database. Trip history stays in this browser.

Try the full flow

  1. Select a pickup and hospital on Overview.
  2. Toggle traffic or close a road to compare routes.
  3. Dispatch a unit and play the accelerated simulation.
  4. Inspect A* explorer and export the trip history.

Inspired by the feature set of Lusan Sapkota’s Ambulance Tracking System. AmbuTrack is an original implementation, with A* pathfinding as its main learning focus.
